statements.quote: Substantial exclusions were applied based on pre-registered quality criteria: 1) participants who completed the study multiple times were flagged based on repeated MTurk worker IDs or coordinated submissions from the same IP address. Only the first valid submission was retained for such cases, 2) participants with fewer than 3 logged interactions or completed the experiment in less than 3 minutes were excluded, as this indicated minimal engagement with the AI system, and 3) submissions flagged by research assistants for bot-like behavior, nonsensical content, or clear inattention were excluded.
statements.locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 8), Section 4.2, Participants, exclusion-criteria paragraph

statements.quote: The study was conducted entirely online through a custom web application.
statements.locator: PDF p. 9 (journal p. 8), Section 4.1, Study design

statements.quote: You will be creating a user persona and scenario for a mobile app designed to help local gardeners trade seeds and produce. A user persona is a fictional character representing a typical user of the app. Your task is to create: (1) A detailed user persona including name and demographics; and (2) A scenario describing how this persona would use the app in a realistic situation.
statements.locator: PDF p. 11 (journal p. 10), Section 4.3, Task and material, printed task brief

statements.quote: Each condition was implemented as a distinct interface configuration within the same web application, using identical underlying AI capabilities (Gemini 2.5 Flash-Lite (preview release 09/2025), accessed through OpenRouter as google/gemini-2.5-flash-lite-preview-09–2025, with condition-specific system prompts (see Appendix A)).
statements.locator: PDF p. 11 (journal p. 10), Section 4.4, Experimental conditions, reference to Appendix A

statements.quote: To capture the nature of engagement, interactions were analyzed as qualitative measures and classified into dialogue act categories (PROPOSE, ELABORATE, CRITIQUE, ACCEPT, REJECT, EDIT, REQUEST_CLARIFICATION, SUGGEST_ALTERNATIVE) using an LLM (Gemma-3-27B) with a structured coding scheme (see Appendix B).
statements.locator: PDF pp. 13-14 (journal pp. 12-13), Section 4.5.3, Process features measures; sentence continues across pages

statements.quote: We validated the LLM coding against a hand-coded subsample (Section 4.6; full results in Section 5.6 and Appendix C).
statements.locator: PDF p. 14 (journal p. 13), Section 4.5.3, reference to validation results in Appendix C

statements.quote: One author hand-coded all 150 turns, blinded to the LLM labels, using the same codebook the LLM received. We report Cohen’s κ overall and per dialogue-act category in Section 5.6 and the full sample of coded turns in Appendix C.
statements.locator: PDF p. 15 (journal p. 14), Section 4.5.6, Dialogue-act coding validation; claim about the full sample in Appendix C

statements.quote: Per-category values are in Appendix C: agreement is near-perfect for the structural ACCEPT act (κ = .81) and fair-to-moderate for the remaining, free-text categories (κ = .12 to .47), several of which have small cell counts.
statements.locator: PDF p. 22 (journal p. 21), Section 5.6, Dialogue-act coding validation

notes: Checked against the complete saved journal article: all 112,405 characters of the markdown were read in consecutive chunks, including references and Appendices A-C, and the relevant statements were verified by extracting the PDF text with pymupdf. PDF p. 1 is the publisher cover; journal page numbers are one lower. Quotes are transcribed from the PDF with whitespace normalized and discretionary line-end soft hyphens removed; the coding-scheme sentence spanning PDF pp. 13-14 is rejoined around the intervening table. The explicit Data availability statement on PDF p. 27 says the datasets are not public and are available from the corresponding author on reasonable request. This applies to the single randomized study S1. No request was sent. The form data_and_code fields data_url and code_url are both empty. No repository URL, dataset DOI, code-release URL, preregistration registry or identifier, or separate supplementary-file link was found in the article or appendices. The quality-criteria preregistration claim has no date, registry, or link. Appendix A prints system prompts and a task brief; Appendix B prints a dialogue-act coding scheme with illustrative examples. Section 4.5.6 claims that Appendix C contains the full sample of coded turns, but PDF p. 32 contains only a validation summary and Table C1, with category-level counts and agreement coefficients. It provides neither the coded-turn rows nor participant identifiers, assignments, scores, or participant texts. The table has eight dialogue-act categories; its n=149 is the number of coded turns underlying aggregate agreement, not a public participant dataset. Section 5.8 is an internal section of supplementary analyses, not an external supplement. Software and data-curation author credits do not constitute a code or data release. No relevant deposit was identified in the recorded repository searches. Broad surname searches were narrowed rather than exhaustively paginated; the narrower DataCite and Zenodo author searches were inspected completely. No paper-specific repository identifier was available for a files/children inventory, and no participant data file was downloaded or read. Unrelated repository search results and the publisher article are not counted as deposits. All network requests used Python urllib with User-Agent atlas-screening/0.1 and no credentials. The publisher landing page was blocked by an HTTP 403 bot check, so publisher-only supplementary files remain unverified; no login, account creation, access request, or bot-check bypass was attempted. Accordingly, no confirmed public data can resolve the form final.open_items concerning unprinted arm means and uncertainty estimates, Figure 7 bootstrap intervals and p values, direct arm-versus-arm diversity contrasts and permutation-null means, deduplicated randomized counts, or exclusions by arm and reason. Participant outcome rows with arm labels, raw persona/scenario texts with participant identifiers, and allocation/exclusion documentation would be needed. Confidence is high in the explicit on-request classification; the publisher access limitation is retained rather than interpreted as proof that no supplement exists.
